s6.title: Heat Health & Rights
s6.subtitle: Evidence-backed public health guidance and worker advisory facts.
s6.emergency_desc: If someone collapses, vomits, or shows confusion, call emergency services immediately. Source: NDMA & Tamil Nadu Health Guidelines. Call 112 for national emergency or 108 for ambulance.
s6.symptoms_source: Source: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) & NIOSH Public Health Guidelines
s6.symptoms_content: Heat Exhaustion: heavy sweating, weakness, cold pale skin, fast weak pulse, nausea. Move to a cool shaded area, loosen clothes, sip cool water. Heat Stroke: body temperature above 103°F (39.4°C), hot red dry or damp skin, rapid strong pulse, confusion, dizziness, unconsciousness. Heat stroke is a medical emergency: call 112 or 108 immediately and cool person with water/cloths while waiting.
s6.hydration_content: Drink 1 cup (240 ml) of water every 15–20 minutes in hot weather, even if you are not thirsty. Do not wait until you feel thirsty. For shifts longer than 2 hours of heavy sweating, take electrolyte solutions or ORS.
s6.rights_source: Source: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) Heatwave Advisory (July 2025)
s6.rights_content: The NDMA advisory asks delivery and gig platforms not to penalize workers for resting during extreme heat (11:00 AM to 4:00 PM) and recommends shade and water stations. Note: Stated as an advisory guideline, not a statutory law.

s3.least_bad_hours_desc: For heavy construction and farm tasks, schedule the heaviest physical labour during early morning (6:00–9:00 AM) or late evening (5:00–7:00 PM) to avoid peak heat while safeguarding daily earnings.
s4.cooling_break_prompt: You have been active for 90 minutes. NDMA heat advisory urges a 15-minute cooling rest in shade to prevent heat stroke.
s4.cooling_break_disclaimer: Personal safety reminder. Operates offline; does not sync to delivery platform ratings or apps.
s4.ors_prompt: Electrolyte Prompt: Shift exceeding 2 hours or extreme heat. Plain water alone is not enough; drink ORS or salted lemon water to prevent heat cramps.
s4.ors_source: Source: NIOSH 2016 Occupational Exposure Criteria & NDMA guidelines. Note: Platforms and municipal bodies are advised to provide clean drinking water and ORS.

honesty.title: Health Before Hustle
honesty.content: Resting during dangerous heat is biological protection, not laziness. Rest protects your kidneys and brain so you can work tomorrow.

s6.women_source: Source: NDMA Heatwave Action Plan & Public Health Guidelines
s6.women_content: Restricting fluid intake due to locked or distant public toilets during heatwaves severely increases the risk of heat exhaustion and kidney/UTI infections. Public health guidelines urge municipal corporations and platforms to ensure clean, accessible toilets and cool water points for all women workers.

s6.triage_subtitle: Check if the worker has any of these critical danger symptoms:
s6.triage_q2: Hot, dry skin OR stopped sweating in high heat
s6.triage_q4: Rapid, pounding heart rate or heavy breathing
s6.triage_q5: Loss of consciousness, seizures, or fainting
s6.triage_danger: CRITICAL DANGER: Possible Heat Stroke! Call 108 immediately. Move worker to shade, loosen clothing, and pour cool water over head and body.
s6.triage_safe: No critical emergency signs checked. Continue frequent hydration, ORS, and resting in shade as advised.
